title: Who Holds the Keys?

claims.text: The browser is the user's doorway to an open network; control of that interface matters.
Firefox helped defend an open, customizable web; it did not invent the open internet. Local storage alone does not establish inspectability or control.
Behavior and inferred preferences accumulate under platform control and influence later recommendations.
Users have some feed controls; the wider ranking and inference machinery remains platform-managed.
The LLM processes supplied context and proposes actions; surrounding software manages tools, durable state and controls.
The illustrated harness stops before publishing for explicit user review.
Readable lessons preserved by the harness shape later context without necessarily retraining the LLM.
Inspecting, correcting, removing and governing the growing working system makes ownership practical.
Rented model intelligence need not transfer ownership of the persistent working system, just as buying electricity does not transfer the toaster.

sections.title: Invitation
sections.purpose: Invite the listener into a story about control of the interface.
lyrics: Come closer.
Let me take you back.
This story starts with a window—
And a fight for the view.

visual.description: Old browser frame opens; a window becomes the recurring doorway motif.
actions: Hold empty window through instrumental introduction

sections.title: A doorway you can change
sections.purpose: Show how open code and practical customization shift user control.
lyrics: Back when the web was young,
Two giants fought to frame the view.
Netscape faced Explorer,
For the window we looked through.
Netscape opened up its code,
Let more hands inside the frame.
Mozilla kept the work alive;
Then Firefox stepped into the game.
Add a button. Block the tracking.
Make the browser fit your day.
Look beneath the painted surface,
Change the way the pieces play.
More eyes checking all the wiring,
More hands working at the seams.
The doorway had a handle
On our side of the screen.
hook: Who decides what you can see?
Let me look. Let me change it.
Leave the final say with me.

visual.description: Netscape and Explorer frames compete, then a separate Netscape → Mozilla → Firefox lineage appears. The user installs an extension, blocks tracking requests, changes appearance and opens source. A handle appears on the user's side.
actions: Snap extension into toolbar on click
Stop tracking tiles at privacy control

sections.title: Your actions build their picture of you
sections.purpose: Make activity → inference → ranking → next experience visible and show the platform-owned accumulating asset.
lyrics: Instagram: a friend's new painting,
A little shop across the street.
Good things found between the pictures,
People I still want to see.
I pause. I save. The signals gather,
Build a portrait out of clues.
Next swipe: the feed's rearranging
What gets buried, what breaks through.
Who keeps that sketch? Who gets to use it?
Which hidden dial decides my view?
I can follow, mute, and filter.
Who gets to set the deeper rules?
hook: Who owns what it learns from me?
Let me look. Let me change it.
Leave the final say with me.

visual.description: Browser narrows into phone feed. Friends, music and shop cards offer real value. Pauses and saves form an inferred Outdoors? profile behind the feed; that profile reranks the next cards. Follow, mute and less-of-this controls remain visible while the wider machine sits inside the platform boundary.
actions: Send signal tiles on pause and save
Pull back to reveal platform boundary

sections.title: Show the harness doing something
sections.purpose: Explain the distinct roles of context, LLM proposals, harness tools, checks and human authority using one workshop-page project.
lyrics: Agentic AI, let's build that page
For Friday's workshop. Set the stage.
My harness brings the notes I've made,
The lessons kept from yesterday.
The L-L-M reads that context,
Suggests a plan for what comes next.
The harness calls the tools we choose;
Their answers shape the next few moves.
Check the date. Then test the link.
Show the draft. Give me room to think.
“Less sales pitch. Show what they'll learn.”
The headline changes at my word.
“Keep that lesson. Save the line
Where I can read it back next time.”
Wait for yes to make it live.
Then check the page that's on the site.

visual.description: A workshop-page brief and teaching notes enter HARNESS. Selected context crosses to a separate LLM module; proposed actions return to harness-controlled tools. The page is edited, date and link checked, then publication stops at a user approval gate. Friday is illustrative story dialogue, not an actual event commitment.
actions: Send context packet across provider boundary
Run page-editing tool and feed results back
Stop Publish card at approval gate
Check date and registration link during instrumental space

sections.title: Show what survives the job
sections.purpose: Show readable saved experience shaping the next job without implying a correction retrains the model.
lyrics: Next time that note goes in the brief;
The new page leads with what we'll teach.
One small correction, kept in view,
Now shapes the next thing that we do.
Our notes and methods start to grow.
Who keeps the keys? Who runs the show?
Who reads the record of my days?
Who gets to choose what goes or stays?
I want to see the guesses made,
Correct the ones that went astray.
Choose the tools, decide their reach,
Keep the rules where I can see.
Keep that system where I can change it,
Or trust a platform with the keys?
As more of my work lives inside it,
Who gets to shape what it will be?
hook: Who decides what it can do?
Let me look. Let me change it.
Let me choose the rules it uses.

visual.description: User corrects a hype-heavy workshop headline and explicitly saves the lesson as a readable note outside the LLM. The next job loads that note into context. Contrast provider-managed controls with user inspection, correction, memory removal and permission changes. Model module stays unchanged.
actions: Remove memory and adjust tool permission

sections.title: Make the diagram familiar
sections.purpose: Resolve the ownership question through electricity → LLM supply and appliance → working harness.
spoken: The L-L-M is like the electricity.
Who gets to hold the keys?

visual.description: Freeze harness machinery and strip the music. Match-cut external intelligence supply to electrical supply and user working system to toaster. User chooses bread and dial; toast pops on the beat. Return to harness with notes and controls still accessible.

hook: Let me look. Let me change it.
Leave the final say with me.

reviewNotes: Only the earlier internet verse was positively singled out; preserve it as the strongest base, not an immutable approved final.
Later verse cadence needs another pass; no generated audio or final timeline exists.
Show real user controls and inferred profiles accurately; this is an illustrative social mechanism, not an Instagram backend reconstruction.
Do not imply every correction retrains model weights.
The current workshop page story replaces generic calendar/mail examples.
No final Suno generation action is currently requested.
Cadence-refined r2 preserves the agreed story; exact wording/style are candidates, not founder approval.
Final toaster analogy is spoken for intelligibility. Leave music-only gaps for scene processes; exact timing awaits actual audio.

lyricConstraint.text: Preserve the intended message while freely adapting wording and storytelling for natural musical delivery. User-controlled and platform-owned are conceptual labels, not required literal lyrics. Technical language may stay in planning or supporting visuals.
